result_text:
Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` now counts as mock resources, whatever the rest of the name is. The new test passes; I didn't run the rest of the `codeanalyzer` suite.

In `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java` (lines 393–394), the two "Mock resources" patterns now allow any characters except `/` and `\` after `mock`/`__mock`. They were `[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+`, which required at least one character after `mock` and only ASCII letters, digits, `_`, `-` and space. That is why plain `mock/`, `mock.data/`, `mock(old)/` and `mock-größe/` were missed. Matching stays inside one folder name, so `remock/`, `demo/`, `mock.java` and `mockery.java` are still not test code.

Windows paths already worked: the existing path matching also tries the pattern against a path with its backslashes swapped for forward slashes, so no change was needed there.

I added `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/MockFolderConventionTest.java`. It checks each of these folder names with both `/` and `\` separators:
- **New cases:** `mock`, `mock.data`, `mock(old)`, `mock-größe`, `mock模拟`.
- **Previously matching cases:** `mocks`, `__mocks__`, `mock-data`, `mock_data`, `mock data`, `mockStore`.

It also checks that `remock/`, `demo/`, `src/main/java/`, `mock.java` and `mockery.java` stay out of test scope.

I didn't commit anything.
